title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
abstract: arXiv:2611.23216v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity. We tracked GitHub pull requests of 297 Fable 5 users before, during, and after the suspension. We used 8,908 developers who stayed on Opus 4.8 all the time as the control group. translated_title: 更高得分的编码模型并没有完成更多工作
translated_abstract: 新的编码模型以编码基准测试的分数提升作为宣传卖点。然而，目前尚无研究检验在这些基准测试中得分更高的模型是否真的能完成更多实际工作。2026年6月12日，一项美国出口管制指令禁止访问Claude Fable 5达19天，迫使用户切换到其他模型。在此期间，大多数前Fable 5用户切换到了Opus 4.8（该模型在SWE-Bench Pro上比Fable 5低11分）。我们将这次停用视为一个自然实验：人员和项目保持不变，只有模型发生了变化，因此我们可以分离出Fable 5对用户生产力的影响。我们跟踪了297名Fable 5用户在停用前、停用期间和停用后的GitHub拉取请求（pull request），并以8,908名始终使用Opus 4.8的开发者作为对照组。此外，我们还在2026年停用前后的五次模型升级中重复了这一比较（涉及1,208名开发者和15,442个拉取请求）。
tldr: 该研究利用美国出口管制导致Claude Fable 5被停用19天的自然实验，发现在编码基准测试中得分更高的模型（Fable 5）相比得分较低的模型（Opus 4.8）并未给用户带来更高的实际工作产出，揭示了基准分数与真实生产力之间的脱节。
en_tdlr: Using the 19-day suspension of Claude Fable 5 under U.S. export controls as a natural experiment, this study finds that coding models with higher benchmark scores (Fable 5) did not deliver more real-world work output than lower-scoring models (Opus 4.8), revealing a disconnect between benchmark scores and actual productivity.
